claims.summary: Cornell lists several genitive plural endings for consonant-declension nouns and conditions them by final sound.

locators.description: Cornell, “Genitive Plural endings,” lines 0–5: introductory scope and endings by final sound.

claims.summary: The four cited forms стаканов, музеев, отцов, and учителей match Cornell’s examples for plain consonant, /y/, ц, and palatalized consonant contexts.

locators.description: Cornell, “Genitive Plural endings,” lines 2–5: exact examples and environments.

claims.summary: стакан → стаканов, музей → музеев, отец → отцов, and учитель → учителей are directly attested in Cornell.
This page addresses #-declension genitive plural endings; the article explicitly excludes unsubstantiated zero-ending classes and exhaustive exception claims.

locators.description: Cornell, “Genitive Plural endings,” lines 0–5; page scope is #-declension forms.
